# s191 — Resolve a next_id-only merge conflict without hand-editing the index

The `next_id` counter in `.slicer/index.json` is a single line that every filing changes. Two branches that each file anything conflict on it at merge time, even when their new ids differ, and the only fix today is a hand edit of tracking JSON, which the project's own rules forbid.

**Findings:** merging s174 into a main whose next_id had moved conflicted only on next_id; resolving it needed a hand edit of index.json · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-05** — Agents upstream feedback 2026-10-05 U8: a run branch changes statuses and files work while main approves drafts. This slice remains the next_id-only driver prerequisite; s217 separately extends that driver to independent item fields, preserving conflicts for incompatible lists and queue reorderings. s185 allocation-floor behavior is shipped. Source: docs/feedback/agents-2026-10-05.md.

**Not in this slice:** allocating ids above a sibling worktree's (that is s185); a renumber command; merging any other tracking file; resolving conflicts in a slice file or the log.

## Why

Hit twice in two days. On 2026-10-04 two filing branches clashed on ids. On 2026-10-05, s174 merged into a `main` that had moved from `next_id` 186 to 189; the one conflict hunk was `"next_id": 189` against `188`, and resolving it took a hand edit of `index.json`. The right answer is always the larger value, so ids are never reused. `slicer setup-git` already installs a merge driver for generated render files, so the project has a place for another one. s185 stops two checkouts allocating the same id; it does not touch this conflict, which remains after s185 because the two branches still add different items.

## Failing tests

1. Given a base, ours and theirs index where only `next_id` differs on both sides, `slicer merge-index BASE OURS THEIRS` writes OURS with the larger `next_id` and exits 0.
2. Given two sides that also differ elsewhere without overlapping, the result keeps both changes and the larger `next_id`.
3. Given overlapping edits to the same item, or conflicts beyond `next_id`, it exits non-zero and leaves the usual conflict markers, so Git reports a normal conflict.
4. `slicer setup-git` configures the driver for `.slicer/index.json` and is idempotent. `slicer check` or `verify` warns when the driver is missing, as it does for the render driver.
5. In a scratch repo, merging two branches that each `add` an item completes with no conflict and `slicer check` is clean afterwards.

## Implement

Add the driver and have `setup-git` register it in the repository's Git config and attributes, next to the existing render driver. The driver runs a three-way merge of the file and, when the only remaining conflict is the `next_id` line, resolves it to the larger number. Anything else stays a normal conflict.
